options.name: auth
options.description: The registered result of the M(crowdstrike.falcon.auth) module, or a dictionary containing the I(access_token) and I(cloud) keys. If provided, the I(client_id), I(client_secret), I(member_cid), and I(cloud) options are ignored. Useful when needing to make multiple API calls to avoid rate limiting issues.

options.name: client_id
options.description: The CrowdStrike API client ID to use. See the L(Falcon documentation,https://falcon.crowdstrike.com/documentation/46/crowdstrike-oauth2-based-apis#understanding-api-clients) for more information about API clients. The C(FALCON_CLIENT_ID) environment variable can also be used.

options.name: client_secret
options.description: The CrowdStrike API secret that corresponds to the client ID. See the L(Falcon documentation,https://falcon.crowdstrike.com/documentation/46/crowdstrike-oauth2-based-apis#understanding-api-clients) for more information about API clients. The C(FALCON_CLIENT_SECRET) environment variable can also be used.

options.name: cloud
options.description: The CrowdStrike cloud region to use. All clouds are automatically discovered if not specified, except for the C(us-gov-1) cloud. The C(FALCON_CLOUD) environment variable can also be used.

options.name: comment
options.description: A comment associated with the rule change.

options.name: description
options.description: A description for the correlation rule.

options.name: ext_headers
options.description: Extended headers that are prepended to the default headers dictionary.

options.name: member_cid
options.description: The CrowdStrike member CID for MSSP authentication. See the L(Falcon documentation,https://falcon.crowdstrike.com/documentation/46/crowdstrike-oauth2-based-apis#understanding-api-clients) for more information about API clients. The C(FALCON_MEMBER_CID) environment variable can also be used.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the correlation rule. Required when creating a new rule and I(rule_id) is not provided. Used to look up an existing rule when I(rule_id) is not specified.

options.name: notifications
options.description: List of notification configurations for the rule.

options.name: operation
options.description: Scheduling configuration for the rule. Required when creating a new rule.

options.name: publish
options.description: Whether to publish the rule version after a create or update operation. When C(true), the module will retrieve the latest rule version and publish it.

options.name: rule_id
options.description: The ID of an existing correlation rule. Preferred for identifying existing rules during update or delete operations. If provided with I(state=present), the module will update the existing rule. If provided with I(state=absent), the module will delete the rule by ID.

options.name: search
options.description: Search criteria for the correlation rule. Required when creating a new rule.

options.name: severity
options.description: The severity level of the rule. Valid values: C(10) (informational), C(30) (low), C(50) (medium), C(70) (high), C(90) (critical).

options.name: state
options.description: The desired state of the correlation rule. C(present) ensures the rule exists with the specified configuration. C(absent) ensures the rule does not exist.

options.name: status
options.description: The operational status of the rule. C(active) enables the rule. C(inactive) disables the rule without deleting it.

options.name: tactic
options.description: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic associated with the rule.

options.name: technique
options.description: The MITRE ATT&CK technique associated with the rule.

options.name: trigger_on_create
options.description: Whether the rule triggers on creation. Only applicable when creating a new rule.

options.name: user_agent
options.description: Custom User-Agent string to use for requests to the API. The user agent string is prepended to the default user agent string (C(crowdstrike-ansible/<version>)). See L(RFC 7231,https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-5.5.3) for more information. The C(FALCON_USER_AGENT) environment variable can also be used.
